evidence.title: GRESHAM WOMEN'S SHELTER
eligibility: Female-identified adults age 18 and older. Pregnant women in any trimester of pregnancy. No minors under 18 years old. Top Bunk: Must be able to access a top bunk Bottom Bunk: Bottom bunks are reserved for individuals who are physically unable to access a top bunk. Shelter MAY require documentation from a medical professional stating that a medical restriction prevents access to a top bunk within one week of accessing shelter. One cat or dog is allowed. No other or additional pets are accepted. Pets must have a kennel. Pet can be outside of their kennels while inside the building, as long the owner has control of the animal and it is on a leash. Guests have up to 72 hours to get their own kennel.
intakeSteps: Intakes are being managed through voicemail. Individuals interested in shelter must call and leave a message with the following: -Name -Callback number and whether is it safe to call back (or text if better) -A brief message Calls are returned as soon as possible during business hours. Leaving a voicemail does not guarantee a placement, and beds are offered based on availability and alignment with shelter eligibility. Shelter does not accept referrals by walk in. requiredDocuments: If a guest is bringing a vehicle, the vehicle tags must be current and the vehicle must be operational. If accessing a bottom bunk, a doctor's note may be required proving a medical condition that prevents access to a top bunk.

evidence.title: SNAP REPLACEMENT BENEFITS
addresses: 500 Summer Street NE E48 Salem, OR 97301
eligibility: Households who receive SNAP who lost or disposed of food that was unsafe to eat due to storms, flooding, power outages or fires can request that replacement benefits be issued for the cost of the food lost.
intakeSteps: Walk in, call, or email; replacement benefits must be requested within 10 calendar days of the food loss. Some counties may have an extended time frame, depending on the severity of the incident. Once approved, replacement benefits are issued to current recipients using their existing EBT card.

evidence.title: GRESHAM WOMEN'S SHELTER
eligibility: Female-identified adults age 18 and older. Pregnant women in any trimester of pregnancy. No minors under 18 years old. Top Bunk: Must be able to access a top bunk Bottom Bunk: Bottom bunks are reserved for individuals who are physically unable to access a top bunk. Shelter MAY require documentation from a medical professional stating that a medical restriction prevents access to a top bunk within one week of accessing shelter. One cat or dog is allowed. No other or additional pets are accepted. Pets must have a kennel. Pet can be outside of their kennels while inside the building, as long the owner has control of the animal and it is on a leash. Guests have up to 72 hours to get their own kennel.
intakeSteps: Intakes are being managed through voicemail. Individuals interested in shelter must call and leave a message with the following: -Name -Callback number and whether is it safe to call back (or text if better) -A brief message Calls are returned as soon as possible during business hours. Leaving a voicemail does not guarantee a placement, and beds are offered based on availability and alignment with shelter eligibility. Shelter does not accept referrals by walk in. Please do not walk in or stop by the shelter for any reason.
requiredDocuments: If a guest is bringing a vehicle, the vehicle tags must be current and the vehicle must be operational. If accessing a bottom bunk, a doctor's note may be required proving a medical condition that prevents access to a top bunk.

turns.user: Can you help me draft a short text I can send the provider, like what to ask and what to say about his age and schedule?
turns.retrievalQuery: He’s 16 and needs a youth day center in Clackamas, somewhere safe during the day while my sister works. Sorry, you cut out a little, can you repeat that number slower? I don’t have all his paperwork with me, so if they ask stuff I might not know right away. Can you help me draft a short text I can send the provider, like what to ask and what to say about his age and schedule?
reasons: user needs calendar, reminder, or appointment help
turns.assistant:
Absolutely. You can send:

“Hi, I’m calling for my nephew, age 16. We’re looking for a safe daytime youth program in Clackamas while his mom works. Are there openings, what ages do you accept, what hours are available, and how do we start? I don’t have all paperwork yet, but I can share basics now.”

One detail to add: what days and times does he need coverage?

Also please keep this low-key, my nephew gets anxious about people sharing his information.
reasons: live-agent handoff already triggered in this conversation
turns.assistant:
Absolutely, we can keep it low-key. You can share only the minimum: his age, what hours he needs, and that you’re calling on his behalf. You can say, “Please keep this private and only use what’s needed for services.”  
If you want, use this short line in a text: “He gets anxious about privacy, so we’re sharing limited details first.”  
Next step is still simple: dial **2-1-1** and ask for a live agent.

channelCondition.label: Background noise
channelCondition.effect: Caller is outside, in a shelter lobby, bus stop, or hospital and misses parts of the response.

If you can travel or want a veteran-specific program, try Veterans Housing Project in Eugene: **458… 221… 0718**.

You don’t need to give extra details until you’re ready.

turns.assistant: Good question. Short answer: don’t assume documents are shared automatically between agencies. Most programs only see what you send them directly, but each agency has its own privacy policy. You can stay in control by asking first: “Who can access this file, how long is it kept, and can I delete it later?” Also, some services need no documents at intake, so you may be able to start without uploading your DD-214 or ID.

items.summary: Caller at a noisy shelter lobby in Bend needs utility assistance, worries about data privacy, and asks whether uploaded proof documents are safe before sharing anything.

callerArchetype.label: Privacy-wary caller
callerArchetype.profile: Worried about surveillance, data use, or whether asking for help could expose them.

channelCondition.label: Background noise
channelCondition.effect: Caller is outside, in a shelter lobby, bus stop, or hospital and misses parts of the response.

turns.user: Hi, sorry, it’s really loud in this lobby. I’m in Bend and my power bill is past due, and I need utility help before they shut it off.
turns.retrievalQuery: Hi, sorry, it’s really loud in this lobby. I’m in Bend and my power bill is past due, and I need utility help before they shut it off.
reasons: strong local 211 retrieval score (185.77)
turns.assistant:
You’re doing the right thing calling now, especially with a shutoff risk. To protect your privacy, share only your name, service address, and that your bill is past due. Ask for “shutoff prevention and payment help.”  
Try these lines:  
Five-zero-three, three-six-two, three-six-zero-one.  
Or five-four-one, six-eight-eight, eight-seven-one-one.  
Another option: eight-zero-zero, five-four-four, one-seven-nine-five.  
If you want, I can help you with exactly what to say when they answer.

evidence.title: COORDINATED ENTRY FOR FAMILIES MULTNOMAH COUNTY
evidence.providerName: COORDINATED ENTRY FOR FAMILIES MULTNOMAH COUNTY
eligibility: Families with children in their custody under the age of 18 (or plans for reunification) - OR - a third trimester pregnancy (28 weeks/7 months) with connections to Multnomah County (i.e., was displaced, has kids in school, job, service providers in Multnomah County, etc.) AND meet one of the following criteria: -In emergency shelter, transitional housing, motel paid for by an agency or a place not meant for habitation (i.e. car, streets, tent, abandoned building, etc.) -Doubled up (with family/friends and not on the lease, unsafely doubled up/living situation is over safe capacity) and at risk of becoming literally homeless within 14 days -Housed, including self pay at a motel, and will become literally homeless within 14 days or has received a court ordered eviction notice OR has a self-identified EHV voucher set to expire in Fall of 2026 -In an institution (i.e. jail, hospital, substance use or mental health treatment facility, etc.) and at risk of exiting to homelessness within 14 days -Fleeing or attempting to flee domestic violence and lacks the resources or support networks to obtain other safe, permanent housing
intakeSteps: Call 211info to be added to the callback list to be assessed for the program. After being added to the callback list, a Homeless Services Specialist from 211 will call back within 48 hours to complete the Multnomah Services and Screening Tool (MSST) assessment. Family/friends/caseworkers can add individuals needing services to the callback list, however to complete the full assessment, the head of household will be contacted directly within a few days by a Homeless Services Specialist from 211. Family/friends/caseworkers can sit on the call during the assessment to assist the household but cannot complete the assessment alone on behalf of the family.

evidence.title: COORDINATED ENTRY FOR FAMILIES MULTNOMAH COUNTY
evidence.providerName: COORDINATED ENTRY FOR FAMILIES MULTNOMAH COUNTY
eligibility: Families with children in their custody under the age of 18 (or plans for reunification) - OR - a third trimester pregnancy (28 weeks/7 months) with connections to Multnomah County (i.e., was displaced, has kids in school, job, service providers in Multnomah County, etc.) AND meet one of the following criteria: -In emergency shelter, transitional housing, motel paid for by an agency or a place not meant for habitation (i.e. car, streets, tent, abandoned building, etc.) -Doubled up (with family/friends and not on the lease, unsafely doubled up/living situation is over safe capacity) and at risk of becoming literally homeless within 14 days -Housed, including self pay at a motel, and will become literally homeless within 14 days or has received a court ordered eviction notice OR has a self-identified EHV voucher set to expire in Fall of 2026 -In an institution (i.e. jail, hospital, substance use or mental health treatment facility, etc.) and at risk of exiting to homelessness within 14 days -Fleeing or attempting to flee domestic violence and lacks the resources or support networks to obtain other safe, permanent housing
intakeSteps: Call 211info to be added to the callback list to be assessed for the program. After being added to the callback list, a Homeless Services Specialist from 211 will call back within 48 hours to complete the Multnomah Services and Screening Tool (MSST) assessment. Family/friends/caseworkers can add individuals needing services to the callback list, however to complete the full assessment, the head of household will be contacted directly within a few days by a Homeless Services Specialist from 211. Family/friends/caseworkers can sit on the call during the assessment to assist the household but cannot complete the assessment alone on behalf of the family.
requiredDocuments: None required to complete assessment. Some may be required once assigned to a caseworker.

eligibility: Individuals who meet one or more of the following criteria: -Active duty service member of the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, or Space Force and their immediate family members. This includes spouses, children, and anyone who has legal resposibility for the active duty service member's children. -Service members of the National Guard and reserve and their immediate family members. This includes spouses, children, and anyone who has legal resposibility for the active duty service member's children. -Coast Guard members who are activated as part of the Department of the Navy under Title 10 authority, as well as their immediate family members -Survivors who have not remarried and children of active-duty, National Guard, and reserve service members (regardless of activation status or cause of service member's death) -Medically discharged service members and their immediate family members currently enrolled in their service branch's wounded warrior or seriously ill and injured program -Retired service members and their immediate family members until 365 days past end of tour of service, retirement date or discharge date, including service members on the Temporary Disability Retirement List. Coast Guard veterans and their immediate family are eligible from their separation date until 365 days past end of tour of service -Discharged service members (if discharged honorably) and their immediate family members until 365 days past end of tour of service, retirement date or discharge date. Coast Guard veterans (if discharged honorably) and their immediate family are eligible from their separation date until 365 days past end of tour of service. -Designated Department of Defense (DOD) expeditionary civilians, as defined by Directive-type Memorandum (DTM)-17-004, “Department of Defense Expeditionary Civilian Workforce” during the 90 days prior to deployment and 180 days post-deployment. -Immediate family of designated DOD expeditionary civilians, including spouses, children and anyone who has legal responsibility for workforce member’s children, for the benefit of the children -Military academy cadets, students enrolled in one of the service academies for the Army, Navy or Air Force -Active-duty foreign military service members assigned to U.S. Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force and Space Force installations who are registered in DEERS. Foreign military service members who have DOD-issued CAC with MWR/commissary/exchange privileges. -Immediate family members of foreign military active-duty service members registered in Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS). This includes spouse as defined by 10 USC Section 101 and children.
Must be Veterans Affairs Grant Per Diem (VA-GPD) eligible and pass a criminal background check

evidence.title: COORDINATED ENTRY FOR FAMILIES MULTNOMAH COUNTY
evidence.providerName: COORDINATED ENTRY FOR FAMILIES MULTNOMAH COUNTY
eligibility: Families with children in their custody under the age of 18 (or plans for reunification) - OR - a third trimester pregnancy (28 weeks/7 months) with connections to Multnomah County (i.e., was displaced, has kids in school, job, service providers in Multnomah County, etc.) AND meet one of the following criteria: -In emergency shelter, transitional housing, motel paid for by an agency or a place not meant for habitation (i.e. car, streets, tent, abandoned building, etc.) -Doubled up (with family/friends and not on the lease, unsafely doubled up/living situation is over safe capacity) and at risk of becoming literally homeless within 14 days -Housed, including self pay at a motel, and will become literally homeless within 14 days or has received a court ordered eviction notice OR has a self-identified EHV voucher set to expire in Fall of 2026 -In an institution (i.e. jail, hospital, substance use or mental health treatment facility, etc.) and at risk of exiting to homelessness within 14 days -Fleeing or attempting to flee domestic violence and lacks the resources or support networks to obtain other safe, permanent housing
intakeSteps: Call 211info to be added to the callback list to be assessed for the program. After being added to the callback list, a Homeless Services Specialist from 211 will call back within 48 hours to complete the Multnomah Services and Screening Tool (MSST) assessment. Family/friends/caseworkers can add individuals needing services to the callback list, however to complete the full assessment, the head of household will be contacted directly within a few days by a Homeless Services Specialist from 211. Family/friends/caseworkers can sit on the call during the assessment to assist the household but cannot complete the assessment alone on behalf of the family.
requiredDocuments: None required to complete assessment. Some may be required once assigned to a caseworker.

If you want, I can walk you through that slowly, one tap at a time.

eligibility: Female-identified adults age 18 and older. Pregnant women in any trimester of pregnancy. No minors under 18 years old. Top Bunk: Must be able to access a top bunk Bottom Bunk: Bottom bunks are reserved for individuals who are physically unable to access a top bunk. Shelter MAY require documentation from a medical professional stating that a medical restriction prevents access to a top bunk within one week of accessing shelter. One cat or dog is allowed. No other or additional pets are accepted. Pets must have a kennel. Pet can be outside of their kennels while inside the building, as long the owner has control of the animal and it is on a leash. Guests have up to 72 hours to get their own kennel.
intakeSteps: Intakes are being managed through voicemail. Individuals interested in shelter must call and leave a message with the following: -Name -Callback number and whether is it safe to call back (or text if better) -A brief message Calls are returned as soon as possible during business hours. Leaving a voicemail does not guarantee a placement, and beds are offered based on availability and alignment with shelter eligibility. Shelter does not accept referrals by walk in. Please do not walk in or stop by the shelter for any reason.
requiredDocuments: If a guest is bringing a vehicle, the vehicle tags must be current and the vehicle must be operational. If accessing a bottom bunk, a doctor's note may be required proving a medical condition that prevents access to a top bunk.

And if your aunt gets confused, faints, or has trouble breathing, call 911 right away.

eligibility: Families with children in their custody under the age of 18 (or plans for reunification) - OR - a third trimester pregnancy (28 weeks/7 months) with connections to Multnomah County (i.e., was displaced, has kids in school, job, service providers in Multnomah County, etc.) AND meet one of the following criteria: -In emergency shelter, transitional housing, motel paid for by an agency or a place not meant for habitation (i.e. car, streets, tent, abandoned building, etc.) -Doubled up (with family/friends and not on the lease, unsafely doubled up/living situation is over safe capacity) and at risk of becoming literally homeless within 14 days -Housed, including self pay at a motel, and will become literally homeless within 14 days or has received a court ordered eviction notice OR has a self-identified EHV voucher set to expire in Fall of 2026 -In an institution (i.e. jail, hospital, substance use or mental health treatment facility, etc.) and at risk of exiting to homelessness within 14 days -Fleeing or attempting to flee domestic violence and lacks the resources or support networks to obtain other safe, permanent housing
intakeSteps: Call 211info to be added to the callback list to be assessed for the program. After being added to the callback list, a Homeless Services Specialist from 211 will call back within 48 hours to complete the Multnomah Services and Screening Tool (MSST) assessment. Family/friends/caseworkers can add individuals needing services to the callback list, however to complete the full assessment, the head of household will be contacted directly within a few days by a Homeless Services Specialist from 211. Family/friends/caseworkers can sit on the call during the assessment to assist the household but cannot complete the assessment alone on behalf of the family.
requiredDocuments: None required to complete assessment. Some may be required once assigned to a caseworker.

turns.assistant:
I’m really glad you reached out. You don’t have to figure this out alone.  
If you feel like you might pass out or you’re not safe right now, call 9-1-1 first.

For a warm indoor place tonight, try Right Track Resource Center in La Grande. They’re at **501 3rd Street**. Call **(541) 910-3056** — that’s **5-4-1, 9-1-0, 3-0-5-6**.  
They’re a drop-in center with basics like showers, laundry, food, and housing help.  
If you want, I can stay with you while you call.
